subject: MedVerify — follow-up: private hosting constraints & next validation steps
messages:
From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
To: Elena Morales <emorales@medverify.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 24 Nov 2026 16:05:00 -0800
Subject: MedVerify — follow-up: private hosting constraints & next validation steps

Hi Elena — thanks again for taking time today. Quick recap from our side and proposed next steps so your security and infra teams have something concise to work against.

What we heard (pain + constraints)
- Regulatory driver: PHI residency requirement — primary requirement is that all customer PHI must remain in a US-only VPC with no egress to third-party regions.
- Air-gap consideration: for audit-scope workloads (P1), you prefer an air-gapped appliance or isolated host with outbound controls (no internet egress from model serving nodes).
- Network topology: you run through a perimeter NGFW + private transit; preferred connection options are either:
  1) Private VPC peering with strict SCTP/TCP port allowlist, or
  2) A dedicated VPN with limited subnets and static routes.
- Ops constraint: you require tooling to fetch audit logs (token / request traces) for 180 days and a push of those logs to your SIEM (Splunk).

Goals we aligned on
- Validate a technical approach that satisfies residency + egress controls within 2 weeks.
- Have Redwood provide a minimal-hosting architecture diagram and an example firewall rule set for your network team to review.
- Security to review our SOC 2 snapshot and confirm whether it maps to your control set (we will redact customer data).

Proposed next steps (owners & ETA)
- Redwood: deliver a 1-page architecture diagram and a minimal port / route allowlist. Deliverable: medverify-network-gw-diagram_v1.pdf. Owner: Karthik. ETA: 2026-11-26 EOD.
- MedVerify: confirm which workloads must be fully air-gapped (P1 list). Owner: Elena / MedVerify IT. ETA: 2026-11-27.
- Redwood Security: send redacted SOC 2 snapshot and mapping notes. Owner: Ben. ETA: 2026-11-25.
- Joint: schedule a 45-min technical deep-dive with MedVerify infra & security to validate rules and SIEM export. Proposed window: week of 11/30. Owner: Laura to coordinate.

Attachments: I’ve attached the SOC 2 snapshot (redacted) and a placeholder diagram that Karthik will update after this thread.

Questions for you now (so we can prep):
1) Do you prefer VPN over peering for the initial pilot, or should we prepare both patterns?
2) What SIEM ingestion method does your security team prefer: S3 push, syslog over TLS, or API pull?

If that all looks right I’ll route the two deliverables and we can lock the deep-dive slot.

Thanks,
Jonas Weber
Senior Solutions Architect | Redwood Inference
jonas.weber@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0142

--
Attachment: redwood-soc2-snapshot-redacted.pdf (pdf, 120KB)
From: Elena Morales <emorales@medverify.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
Cc: MedVerify IT <it@medverify.com>, procurement@medverify.com
Date: Wed, 25 Nov 2026 09:14:00 -0800
Subject: Re: MedVerify — follow-up: private hosting constraints & next validation steps

Jonas — thanks for the crisp summary; this matches our notes. Quick clarifications:

- P1 workloads: the following services must be considered P1 for air-gap: patient-matching, claims-normalization, and the API gateway that touches raw PHI. I’ll send a short list by today EOD.
- Preferred connection: procurement historically prefers VPN for initial pilots since it avoids cloud-level peering approvals; however, security wants peering for long-term because it reduces transit hops. So yes, please prepare both patterns — prioritize VPN in the deliverable.
- SIEM ingestion: we prefer S3 push of compressed logs (encrypted with KMS key we control).

We’ll need the firewall allowlist and diagram to circulate with our security review. Also, please note our change control requires a maintenance window template for any initial deployment — can you include that in the next doc?

I’m copying MedVerify IT (it@medverify.com) and procurement for visibility.

—Elena Morales
Sr. Director, Security & Compliance | MedVerify
emorales@medverify.com | +1 (617) 555-0199

--
Attachment: medverify-p1-workloads.xlsx (mentioned as incoming)
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Elena Morales <emorales@medverify.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 25 Nov 2026 11:02:00 -0800
Subject: Re: MedVerify — follow-up: private hosting constraints & next validation steps

Elena — appreciated. Uploading the redacted SOC 2 snapshot you saw in the meeting (attached) and a short mapping doc that highlights controls relevant to residency and access control. I flagged items that typically require customer attestations so your audit team can assess coverage quickly.

Notes:
- The SOC 2 snapshot is redacted to remove customer-specific evidence. It contains control/testing windows and the control owner. If you need deeper artifacts (e.g., VPC flow logs samples) we can put those in a controlled share under NDA.
- We will include a maintenance-window template in the architecture doc per your request.

Next: Karthik, please take the diagram to version 2 with VPN-first and peering appendices and include an s3-push SIEM example. Laura, please propose 3 slots for the week of 11/30 for the deep-dive; we should include one of our security engineers + a solutions architect.

Ben Carter
Director, Trust & Safety | Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.com

--
Attachment: redwood-soc2-snapshot-redacted.pdf (pdf, 130KB)
From: MedVerify IT <it@medverify.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: Elena Morales <emorales@medverify.com>, procurement@medverify.com
Date: Fri, 28 Nov 2026 09:15:00 -0800
Subject: Re: MedVerify — follow-up: private hosting constraints & next validation steps

Team — thanks. Quick operational confirmations from infra:

1) We will classify patient-matching and claims-normalization as P1; we will send the canonical list by EOD.
2) VPN is preferred for the pilot. One constraint: our VPN terminator only accepts IKEv2 with certificate-based auth (no pre-shared keys). Can Redwood support that mode? If not, we’ll need a short design note.
3) For SIEM: S3 push is fine; we’ll provide a KMS key ARN for encryption. We prefer compressed JSONL per file with a 1GB max object size.
4) Maintenance window: Tuesdays 02:00–04:00 UTC is preferred for initial rollout.

Available for the deep-dive: Mon 11/30 15:00–16:00 PST or Tue 12/01 09:00–10:00 PST. Please confirm which slot works.

—MedVerify IT (ops)
it@medverify.com
